name: MN-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+32 Minneapolis district is among the most Democratic seats in the country
Omar holds a massive financial edge: $1.3M on hand versus Nagel's $47K
No public polls or expert ratings treat the race as competitive
model.rationale: The seat's D+32 lean and Omar's history of roughly 50-point general-election wins make a Republican upset implausible, and her fundraising dominance over Nagel reinforces that picture. Fundamentals point to a margin in the mid-30s or better, with markets and the absence of any competitive signals confirming Safe D status.
model.watch: A late-breaking scandal or an unusually strong independent showing could trim the margin, though the district's lean makes an upset exceedingly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Minneapolis-based MN-05 is one of the most Democratic seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+32. Ilhan Omar has held it since 2019 and has won general elections by roughly 50-point margins. She enters the fall with $1.3 million on hand after raising $5.8 million, while Republican John Nagel has just $47,000 in the bank despite raising $747,000. No outside groups are spending in the race, and an independent candidate lacks any visible funding.

Prediction markets give Omar a 95% chance of winning, and no public polls or expert ratings treat the contest as competitive. Fundamentals point to a margin in the mid-30s or better, consistent with the district's history of lopsided results. The main uncertainty is the size of the win, not the winner, with the seat firmly in the Democratic column.
